question: What primary hormonal shift occurs during the immediate metabolic response to surgical stress?

options.A: Surge in catabolic hormones breaking down tissues
options.B: Increase in anabolic hormones building up muscle
options.C: Drop in adrenal gland cortisol and adrenaline output
options.D: Complete cessation of pancreatic insulin production

explanation: Surgical trauma causes catecholamines, cortisol, and glucagon to spike, driving the breakdown of body stores for rapid energy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h1)

question: Why is a negative nitrogen balance dangerous for a recovering surgical patient?

options.A: It causes an immediate drop in systemic blood pressure
options.B: It stops the liver from filtering metabolic waste products
options.C: It leads to severe muscle wasting and delayed wound healing
options.D: It triggers sudden acute kidney failure within hours

explanation: A negative nitrogen balance means protein breakdown exceeds intake, robbing the body of building blocks needed for tissue repair. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h1)

question: An unintentional weight loss exceeding what percentage over six months signals severe nutritional risk?

options.A: Ten percent of total body weight
options.B: Two percent of total body weight
options.D: Fifty percent of total body weight

explanation: Losing more than ten percent of baseline body weight over half a year indicates significant physiological depletion before surgery. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h2)

question: What does a low serum albumin level primarily indicate in a preoperative patient?

options.A: Excessive daily water consumption diluting the blood
options.B: Visceral protein depletion and chronic systemic inflammation
options.C: High levels of physical fitness and muscle mass
options.D: An acute allergic reaction to hospital food items

explanation: Serum albumin acts as a marker for internal protein stores and drops during periods of prolonged nutritional stress or illness. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h2)

question: A patient complains of mild nausea after advancing from clear liquids to a soft diet post-surgery. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Insert a nasogastric tube immediately for gastric decompression
options.B: Temporarily pause the diet advancement and notify the surgical team
options.C: Force the patient to finish the meal to maintain calorie goals
options.D: Discharge the patient home with anti-nausea medications

explanation: Nausea indicates the gastrointestinal tract is struggling to keep pace, requiring a temporary halt in advancement to prevent vomiting. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h3)

question: Which complication is prevented by implementing early oral feeding protocols after abdominal surgery?

options.A: Chronic autoimmune destruction of pancreatic beta cells
options.B: Rapid accumulation of fluid inside the cranial vault
options.C: Sudden permanent paralysis of the lower extremities
options.D: Loss of gut mucosal integrity and bacterial translocation

explanation: Using the digestive tract early keeps the intestinal lining healthy and stops gut bacteria from crossing into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h3)

question: When is enteral nutrition preferred over parenteral nutrition for surgical patients?

options.A: When the patient has severe intractable vomiting and diarrhea
options.B: When the patient refuses to swallow any medication pills
options.C: When the gastrointestinal tract is functional and accessible
options.D: When there is an absolute mechanical obstruction of the bowel

explanation: Using the gut whenever possible maintains normal physiological function and carries fewer infectious risks than intravenous feeding. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h4)

question: Why must parenteral nutrition solutions be infused through a central venous catheter?

options.A: Peripheral veins cannot absorb water molecules efficiently
options.B: Central catheters prevent all forms of bacterial contamination
options.C: The high concentration of nutrients irritates small peripheral veins
options.D: Central lines deliver medications much faster than peripheral lines

explanation: Parenteral solutions are hyperosmolar and will damage fragile peripheral blood vessels, requiring large central veins to dilute the fluid quickly. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h4)

question: Why must patients who underwent a gastrectomy separate fluid intake from solid meals?

options.A: To allow the pancreas to secrete adequate amounts of insulin
options.B: To prevent rapid gastric emptying and subsequent dumping syndrome
options.C: To ensure the stomach expands back to its original normal size
options.D: To stop the liver from producing excess bile acids during digestion

explanation: Drinking fluids with meals washes food quickly into the small intestine, triggering the uncomfortable symptoms of dumping syndrome. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of dumping syndrome after upper gastrointestinal surgery?

options.A: Sudden swelling of the face and upper extremities
options.B: Complete inability to taste sweet or salty flavors
options.C: Dizziness and palpitations shortly after eating sugary foods
options.D: Severe constipation lasting for more than seven days

explanation: A sudden shift of fluid into the gut due to high sugar loads causes vasomotor symptoms like dizziness, sweating, and rapid heart rate. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h5)

question: A recovering surgical patient eats only a few bites of each meal due to early satiety. What nursing intervention is best?

options.A: Provide small, nutrient-dense meals and snacks throughout the day
options.B: Insist that the patient clean the plate during three large meals
options.C: Stop all food intake and start total parenteral nutrition immediately
options.D: Administer strong appetite stimulants before every scheduled meal

explanation: Grazing on calorie-packed, smaller portions prevents the patient from feeling overwhelmed while meeting their daily nutritional targets. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h6)

question: Which factor is most helpful to include when designing a long-term post-surgical diet plan?

options.A: Strict avoidance of all traditional local home dishes
options.B: Eating only raw vegetables and unprocessed fruits
options.C: Eliminating all dietary fats from daily meal preparation
options.D: The patient's personal and cultural food preferences

explanation: Incorporating familiar foods that the patient enjoys increases compliance and ensures adequate long-term nutritional intake. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T009#GNS227_U7_T009_h6)
